posts.title: Small Classes Foster Curious Questioners
posts.excerpt: A child's hand goes up, then goes back down. In a room of thirty, that hesitation happens dozens of times a day, and it shapes how comfortable a child ever becomes with not knowing something.

posts.title: How Small Classes Boost Student Curiosity
posts.excerpt: A child sits in a room of thirty, has a question forming, and watches it disappear before the hand goes up. Not because the question wasn't good, but because the moment passed and the teacher moved on.

posts.title: Education: The Path to World Peace
posts.excerpt: Wars, conflicts, and violent extremism continue to dominate global headlines, yet the underlying drivers, ignorance, prejudice, and economic desperation, are largely preventable.

posts.title: How Small Classes Encourage Student Questions
posts.excerpt: A child who feels safe raises a hand. A child who feels invisible rarely does. Class size shapes that safety more than almost anything else in a school day.

posts.title: Homeschooling vs Next Gen Schooling
posts.excerpt: Choosing between homeschooling and a modern, next-gen school is one of the biggest decisions a family makes, and it's rarely just about academics.
